approach: In the incline's accelerating frame, add the pseudo force to gravity and take the component of both along the slope; that total is the needed friction force.

steps.text: In the incline's frame, a pseudo force of magnitude ma acts on the block, directed opposite to the incline's acceleration, that is backward and down toward the low end of the slope.
steps.equation: pseudo force = ma, horizontal, opposite to the incline's acceleration

steps.text: Resolve gravity's component along the incline, down the slope.
Resolve the pseudo force's component along the incline; since it points toward the low end, it also adds down the slope.
For the block to stay still relative to the incline, friction must balance the sum of these two down-slope components, acting up the slope.
steps.equation: f = mg sin37° + ma cos37° = m(g·3/5 + a·4/5)

steps.text: Substitute g = 10 m/s² and a = 3 m/s².
steps.equation: f = m(6 + 2.4) = 8.4m N, directed up the incline

final_answer.value: f = 8.4m N, directed up the incline

common_mistakes.text: Ignoring the pseudo force from the incline's own acceleration and using only gravity gives f = 0.6mg = 6m N.
Swapping sin37° and cos37° between the gravity and pseudo-force terms gives f = m(g×4/5 + a×3/5) = 9.8m N, the wrong combination.
